Figure 3A asks what each pair exchanges, before introducing Social Rank. This page shows the three heatmaps separately. [Figure 3B](06_figure3b_tokens_by_rank.qmd) then adds rank differences, and [Figure 3C](07_figure3c_cooperation_gap.qmd) shows the Cooperation GAP. The [assembly page](figure3_assembly.qmd) combines all nine panels with the row headers.

# From directed decisions to exchange cells

Each unordered pair has two transfers, `tokens_sent` and `tokens_received`, both on the original 0–10 allocation scale. The larger transfer is stored as `high` and the smaller as `low`; folding the grid this way puts both orientations of the pair in the same cell. These axes describe the larger and smaller transfer, regardless of which child has higher Social Rank.

The heatmaps use three groups: non-friends, mutual friends, and all asymmetric friendships. Both nomination directions enter the asymmetric heatmap. Each pair appears in two directed rows, so counting both rows doubles every cell count equally and leaves the within-group percentages unchanged.

The next chunk builds two auxiliary tables for panel A from `analysis_dyads`. `heatmap_cells` contains the exchange-cell counts and percentages; `heatmap_regions` sums the percentages within each highlighted region. The heatmap function uses these tables to draw the panels.

```{r heatmap-data}
#| output: false
#| code-summary: "heatmap-data"
```

```{r show-heatmap-regions}
#| code-summary: "show-heatmap-regions"
heatmap_regions
```

The highlighted regions have explicit definitions: both transfers at most one token; one transfer of ten and the other at most five; and both transfers equal to ten. The unequal-exchange region is narrower than a rule based on any difference of at least five tokens.

# Inspect the underlying percentages

The table below lists the five most frequent exchange cells within each relationship group. `high` and `low` give the two heatmap coordinates, and `percent` gives the value drawn in that cell.

```{r inspect-heatmap-percentages}
#| code-summary: "inspect-heatmap-percentages"
heatmap_cells %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  slice_max(percent, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()
```
